answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of non-memory-hard computational proof-of-work per identity to protect the network from sybil-based erosion. The verifier enforces this by checking if each hash output matches a unique, fresh task, like a navigator on a long voyage. While an honest agent pays this base cost once, an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, falling into a canyon of debt as a gale of compute demands sweeps away cheap roots. Fraud triggers a permanent identity burn.
